newsitem.title: USA: SanDisk to invest $45 million in plant.
newsitem.headline: SanDisk to invest $45 million in plant.

text.p: SanDisk Corp. said Monday it will invest $45 million in a joint venture semiconductor manufacturing plant headed by United Microelectronics Corp. in Taiwan.
SanDisk, which makes data, image and audio storage products, said the deal will give it a 10 percent equity stake in the joint foundry venture, the company's third.
The facility is scheduled to start producing limited quantities of semiconductor wafers in late 1998 and will start full monthly production of about 20,000 eight-inch wafers in 1999.

SanDisk said the joint venture is part of its long-term, manufacturing strategy. The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based company already has long-standing manufacturing partnerships with Matsushita Electronics Corp., NEC Corp. and LG Semicon.
SanDisk's stock rose 44 cents to $18.75 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
